ledgerSearch.outcome: The volume-04 voice card names any account of dissent as infection among the known weak passages, which governs the immune system material directly. CTD-0078 requires that the COINTELPRO and Tilly lineages not function as proof of a present threat. CTD-0055 requires that no defensive property be asserted as an accomplished fact. No item forbids the adaptive adversary analysis itself.

findings.summary: The reframing of the audit culture as an adaptive capacity was removed.

evidence.baseline: The audit culture was introduced in earlier chapters as a mechanism for detecting drift and capture. Its deeper function, now visible, is to be the institution's adaptive capacity: the capacity to detect novel forms of attack that the architecture did not anticipate, and to mount responses that the architecture did not pre-specify.
evidence.shipped: The architecture must learn. Regular audits, public incident reports, independent review, sunset clauses, threat modeling, and repair procedures can reveal new failure modes.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped list of practices is excellent and is kept. What went is the reframing, which is the section's argument: a mechanism introduced eleven chapters earlier turns out to have a second and larger function. That kind of late reinterpretation is the payoff of a long structure and it cannot be reconstructed from a list.

findings.summary: The argument that the human architecture is the institution's only defense against unanticipated threats was removed.

evidence.baseline: The developmental culture is not a soft enhancement to the hard architecture. It is the hard architecture's only defense against the threats the hard architecture cannot anticipate. ... The defense against adaptive power is, in the end, a sufficient density of human beings who understand the architecture deeply enough to protect it in forms its builders never specified. There is no shortcut to that density. It is the work of the whole project.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and the voice card's dissent as infection warning read across the immune material.
findings.diagnosis: This is the volume's closing argument for Parts III and V, and it is the reason the book spends a third of its length on people. The card's concern is with treating dissent as infection, which the restoration answers by keeping the shipped statement that critics are not pathogens and by replacing the baseline's vigilance vocabulary with attention and detection. The argument survives, the metaphor is bounded, and the sentence that names the whole project's purpose returns.

debtImpact.note: The organizational resilience lineage is restored in the shipped form, which prefers distributed detection and incident response to a literal immune analogy.

reasoning.note: R-LEDGER-WINS. The immune system material returns as a bounded analogy. The shipped statements that critics are not pathogens, that dissent is not infection, and that participants should not be asked to live in permanent vigilance are kept, and the baseline's vigilance language is reduced to attention and detection throughout.
R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Six em dashes. Four were parenthetical appositives and became comma pairs. Two introduced specifications of the adaptive capacity and became colons.
The audit culture reframing, the three worked examples of distributed detection, the developmental culture argument, and the density close.

openQuestions:
STRUCTURAL RESTORATION BLOCKED ON ROUTE ADJUDICATION, not an editorial judgment. The introduction to PART EIGHT, the running prose between the part label The Scales of the Dragon and the first chapter heading beneath it, compiles into a chapter-start section with its own public route. Restoring the baseline's fuller introduction revives a section whose route was retired, and attempting it broke the build for this part. The introduction has therefore been reverted to its pre-edit state byte for byte and no part introduction anywhere in this volume was touched. Reassigning a canonical route and a reviewed successor is an author-facing continuity decision and this pass has no standing to make it.

WHAT STANDS NOW:

The earlier parts concentrated on constraint and failure. Part VIII turns toward the civic and ecological possibilities those safeguards are meant to protect, while keeping the vision conditional.

WHAT THE BASELINE HAS, punctuation already repaired so it can be pasted in one edit once the route decision is made:

The preceding seven parts were disciplined by a single question: how can Providence be built without becoming what it was designed to replace? That question was necessary, and the rigor it demanded was not optional. But a book that only asks how a thing avoids failure has described a scaffold and never the cathedral the scaffold is for. This part turns, at last, toward what the architecture makes possible. It does not abandon the rigor. It completes it, by letting the reader see, and feel, the civilization that all the careful construction is in service of. We have shown what Providence must not become. Here we show what it could become, if it is built well, and the vision remains conditional throughout.

WHAT THE CURRENT TEXT LOSES: the scaffold and cathedral argument, that a book which only asks how a thing avoids failure has never described what the avoiding is for.

TO RESTORE: the prose change and the continuity change must land together. The section id minted by the restored introduction needs a canonical route and a reviewed successor recorded in publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json in the same edit.

The restored argument says the defense against adaptive power is a sufficient density of people who understand the architecture. That is close to asking participants for permanent alertness, which the shipped text explicitly refuses. Both are restored and both are kept. The reconciliation is the author's.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The section is the volume's hardest ledger case because the card's objection is to a metaphor and the argument the metaphor carries is sound. Bounding the metaphor rather than deleting the argument is what R-LEDGER-WINS actually asks for, and it took the whole of Part VII to see it clearly.
